Checked next to fog-lesser-demon, spark-imp and tower-butcher on the stage at 128 px: the sword and silhouette read clearly.

Kept. Reference pose kept as idle_0; idle_1 is a subtle settle (~2.5% lower, sword tip dipped); spell_0 two-finger seal at the chest with blade lowered, spell_1 seal hand thrust forward in a lunge. Identity and scale consistent.

The dodge blade points forward rather than tucked back - acceptable.
Kept. contact -> down -> passing with forward lean, sword carried low/back, scarf streaming.

Kept with a caveat: meant as the opposite-leg half of the cycle, but the model drew nearly the same leg phases as run-a. Because both legs look alike at game size the 6-frame loop still reads as a run (checked in onion skin and at 128 px); a true leg swap would need a regeneration.

Kept. Clear draw-back at the hip -> full horizontal extension -> blade swept back-left. Anticipation and follow-through share a back-pointing blade, so their silhouettes are similar; the strike in between separates them.

Kept. Low blade -> rising 45-degree backhand with twisted torso -> blade high overhead. Faint red/white fringe seen in the raw preview is in alpha<32 pixels and disappears after alpha cleanup (checked on gray and floor colour).
Kept. Overhead two-hand wind-up -> airborne apex (feet ~108 px above ground at unit 320) -> deep-crouch chop with blade low in front -> recover to guard.
Kept. charge (deep crouch, two-hand blade back) -> dash (longer, lower lunge; silhouette close to charge) -> sweep (full extension, the hero pose) -> finish (blade out to the side/back, chin up).
Kept. hurt_0 recoil with head snapped back and front foot lifted; down_0 lying on his back, head left, sword beside him; getup_0 on one knee with the sword point planted.

processing: Environment: Pillow 11.3.0 in a scratch venv (/tmp/if-action/hero/.venv; python3 -m venv + pip install Pillow), not a repo dependency.
tools/slice_pack.py: alpha cleanup (alpha<=8 -> 0 removes generator noise; alpha>=248 -> 255, the generator writes 250-254 inside bodies).

Split each sheet by 8-connected components on alpha>24 at half resolution; the N largest are poses, smaller fragments merge into the nearest pose by bbox gap; poses ordered left to right; mask dilated 1 px to keep soft edges.

Scale: the sheet's first pose (master combat idle) opaque height -> 320 px (unitHeight); every pose in the sheet uses that factor (0.61-0.86, always a downscale). Resampling LANCZOS in premultiplied alpha (RGBa) to avoid fringes.
Ground line per sheet = bottom of the reference pose; foot y = that line in frame-local px (airborne frames keep their height above it).

Foot x: clips idle/spell/item use the centre between the outer feet on the ground line (thin sword/scarf removed by a 11 px opening); all other clips use the pelvis (centre of mass of the 21 px-eroded body in the belt-to-crotch band), because feet-midpoint made the run body jump +/-100 px between frames. Manual fixes in anchor-overrides.json.
Sword tips (attack1_1, attack2_1, attack3_2, skill_2): extreme opaque pixel in the blade direction, checked by eye in the filmstrips.
Shelf-packed (2 px padding, smallest-area width <= 2048) into hero-action.png; hero-action.json in the agreed shape.
Review previews in /tmp/if-action/hero/preview/ (filmstrip-*, onion-*, contact-sheet, game-scale-on-stage); not in the repo.

v2 run: tools/run_eval.py (candidate metrics, 128 px strip, onion, GIFs), tools/run_solve.py (run anchor dx + runCycle); slice_pack.py gained 'skip' poses, frame aliases, per-sheet 'row-max' ground, two-row ordering and frame-local half-up rounding of foot/tip.

attempts.why: C1a: 9 figures, steadiest upper body (head x range 10.4 px over 8 frames, 5.4 px within frames 4-7 at unit 320), compact stride (~0.55 of standing height at contact), two clean head bobs. No readable near/far leg swap between its halves, so one half is used as a 4-phase step; frames 4-7 chosen because their planted-foot travel per frame (45/62/78 px) is far more even than frames 0-3 (74/37/97). Sword is carried low with the blade pointing down-forward rather than back - consistent in every frame.
C1b: same layout; no leg swap either, head x range 19.8 px, stride ~0.68 of standing height (longer than the 0.55-0.65 target), up frames fully airborne.
C2 half A: good 4 phases but stride ~0.79 of standing height (long sprint), head x range 24 px across both halves.
C2 half B (half A passed as second reference): nearly a copy of half A - legs not swapped; same long stride.
C3 two-row layout: came back with an opaque smoky background instead of transparency.

result.clip: run_0..run_7 = contact, down, passing, up, repeated (run_4..7 alias run_0..3 and share their atlas rects). Fallback chosen because no candidate drew a readable near/far leg swap; the 4 phases are distinct and their spacing was evened by anchor shifts.
result.anchors: pelvis x (as before) plus per-frame dx from tools/run_solve.py (lambda 1): least squares over planted-foot slip (heel for contact->down->passing, toe for passing->up) and cyclic head-x steps; ground = lowest run foot on the sheet.
result.runCycleMeaning: atlas px (unit 320) the root must travel per 8-frame loop so the planted foot does not slide = 8 x 62.0 px/frame (per-step planted-foot backward travel contact->push-off = 185.5 px over 3 of the step's 4 frame intervals; both steps together 371 px over 6 intervals)
result.nonRunFrames: all 25 non-run frames verified pixel-identical to v1 (art, frame-local foot and tip); 3 anchors (idle_0, idle_1, spell_1) pinned with x overrides because rounding moved to frame-local half-up.
